title: Multimodal Conditional Retrieval with High Controllability

problem.claim: Text-based image search struggles to express abstract intentions, while image-based search cannot express specific purposes.

gap.claim: Existing graph search works often provide only a single function, such as content search or style search, rather than jointly capturing content and style intentions.

contributions.claim: CCSR is a multimodal conditional content-style joint retrieval model combining text and image inputs.
The model uses contrastive learning for conditional retrieval, a Mixture-of-Experts system for collaboration among expert systems, and adaptive prompt selection.
StyleCoco is a dataset containing content and style categories for evaluating joint content-style retrieval.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that CCSR is the first conditional retrieval model to apply contrastive learning and that its Mixture-of-Experts system is novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance in conditional style retrieval, content retrieval, and style-content retrieval.
The authors state that the dataset and code will be publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text and image search each have limitations in expressing specific and abstract user intentions.
The work seeks to combine the complementary strengths of text and images to better capture user intentions.
CCSR is proposed with conditional content-style joint retrieval, contrastive learning, Mixture-of-Experts collaboration, and adaptive prompt learning.
StyleCoco is introduced to evaluate joint content-style retrieval.
The authors report state-of-the-art results across conditional style, content, and style-content retrieval tasks.
